notes: Identity: title "Two Conceptions of Subjective Experience" and authors Justin Sytsma and Edouard Machery match the assigned reference. The supplied source identifies a Philsci Archive PDF URL and contains a full primary research manuscript (42 numbered pages, three studies, Appendix and references), not a secondary report or abstract. DOI and journal pagination are not printed in the supplied text; correspondence of assigned journal p.325 to a manuscript page cannot be verified locally. No PDF path was supplied. The locator specifies Study 1 and broadly "Attributions of consciousness to machines", without identifying the mental state, participant group, or contrast. Study 1 contains robot seeing-red and pain tests against the neutral midpoint for both philosophers and non-philosophers, an across-state folk comparison, and factorial analyses. The supplied manuscript uses pp.1–42, so journal p.325 cannot independently resolve the test. Selecting the sole printed d would use metric availability to choose the target rather than an identified contrast. Printed candidate only: the comparison of folk robot seeing-red versus feeling-pain ratings reports t (109)=7.12, p<.001, d = 0.87. Its mutually exclusive final robot groups have N=52 (seeing red) and N=59 (pain), so candidate analytic participant N is 52 + 59 = 111. Random assignment to one of four scenarios establishes exclusivity. These are retained candidates, not assigned row values. Whole-study final groups are 372 philosophers and 231 non-philosophers (372 + 231 = 603), following 68 exclusions from 671 survey completions; 603 is not the sample of the candidate folk robot contrast. Exclusions concern incomplete biographical information or probe misunderstanding. Other robot candidates: philosophers seeing red N=96, p<.01 and pain N=100, p<.005; folk seeing red N=52, p<.005 and pain N=59, p<.005 (each against 4). These midpoint p bounds do not belong to the across-state d. The source supplies d without explicitly naming its standardisation convention. Unassigned replication and reported-success fields are placeholders.
